items.title: Concrete driveways
items.description: New and replacement concrete driveways in Adelaide, reinforced and jointed to carry daily vehicle traffic.
includes: Control joints cut within a day of the pour
items.longDescription: A driveway fails at the base long before it fails at the surface. We excavate to firm ground, compact a crushed rock base, set mesh on chairs so the steel sits inside the slab instead of under it, and cut control joints so the slab cracks where the joint is rather than across the middle.

items.title: Shed and garage slabs
items.description: Level, reinforced slabs for sheds, garages and carports, with edge thickening where the frame loads the slab.
includes: Set-out to the shed supplier's plan
items.longDescription: Shed kits are built to a slab plan, and a slab that is out of square by a few millimetres makes every wall sheet a fight. We set out from the supplier's drawing, check the diagonals before the pour, and thicken the edges where the portal frames bolt down.

items.title: Paths and patios
items.description: Concrete paths, patios and pool surrounds finished with a broom or cove texture for grip.
includes: Falls set away from the house
items.longDescription: Water has to go somewhere. Every path and patio is formed with a fall away from the building, and separated from walls and existing slabs with an expansion joint so the new concrete can move without pushing on the old.

items.title: Exposed aggregate concrete
items.description: Exposed aggregate driveways and entertaining areas, with the stone mix chosen from supplier samples.
includes: Sample selection from the supplier's range
items.longDescription: Exposed aggregate is washed back while the surface is still green to show the stone in the mix. Timing decides the result: too early and stones pull out, too late and the paste will not wash. The slab is sealed once it has cured.

items.title: Coloured concrete
items.description: Through-coloured concrete in oxide tones, for driveways and paths that should not look grey.
includes: Colour mixed through the full slab depth
One batch plant for the whole pour
items.longDescription: Oxide is mixed through the load at the plant, so the colour runs the full depth of the slab and a chip does not show grey. Colour varies between batches, which is why a coloured job is ordered from one plant and poured in one day wherever the size allows.

items.title: Concrete removal and replacement
items.description: Cracked or lifted concrete cut out, removed and replaced on a properly prepared base.
includes: Saw cutting to a clean line
Removal and disposal of the old slab
Base repair before the new pour
items.longDescription: Old concrete usually cracked for a reason: tree roots, a soft base or no joints. We cut the failed section out on a straight line, remove it, fix what caused the failure, and then pour the replacement.

whyUs.heading: Concrete placed to AS 3600 and AS 2870 practice

items.title: Base before concrete
items.description: Topsoil and soft spots come out and a compacted crushed rock base goes in. Concrete bridges nothing: it follows whatever is underneath it.

items.title: Steel where it works
items.description: Mesh is lapped, tied and lifted onto bar chairs so it sits in the upper third of the slab, with the cover the engineer or the standard calls for.

items.title: Joints planned on paper
items.description: Control joint positions are marked on the set-out before the truck is booked, so panels stay close to square and no re-entrant corner is left unjointed.

items.title: Curing is part of the pour
items.description: A curing compound goes on the same day. Concrete that dries too fast in an Adelaide summer dusts and crazes at the surface.

items.question: How thick should a concrete driveway be?
items.answer: For ordinary cars, residential driveways are commonly poured 100 mm thick with steel mesh. Heavier vehicles such as caravans or trucks need a thicker slab and heavier reinforcement.

items.question: Do I need council approval for a new driveway?
items.answer: The part of the driveway on your own land usually does not, but the crossover between the kerb and your boundary belongs to the council and normally needs a permit. Check with your council before any work starts.

items.question: How long before I can drive on new concrete?
items.answer: Foot traffic is generally fine after a day or two. Keep cars off for at least seven days, and heavier vehicles off for longer. Concrete keeps gaining strength for about a month.

items.question: Why does concrete crack?
items.answer: Concrete shrinks as it cures, so some cracking is expected. Control joints are cut into the slab so that the cracking happens neatly inside the joint instead of across the surface.

items.question: Does exposed aggregate need sealing?
items.answer: Yes. A sealer protects the surface from stains and makes it easier to clean. Expect to reseal every few years, depending on traffic and sun.

items.question: Can coloured concrete be matched to an existing slab?
items.answer: Not exactly. Colour depends on the cement, the sand, the weather on the day and how the surface was finished, so a new pour beside an old one will always read slightly differently.
